newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thailand eyes South Asia for trade and investment.
newsitem.headline: Thailand eyes South Asia for trade and investment.

text.p: Deputy Foreign Minister of Thailand Pitak Intrawityanunt said on Monday Bangkok was keen on forging closer economic ties with its western neighbours in South Asia -- Bangladesh, India and Sri Lanka.
"In fact, our government is pursuing the policy of Look West. This is a very important region for trade and investment," Intrawityanunt told Reuters in Dhaka.

"It's a big market. Huge population, huge natural resources and huge potential," said the minister who arrived on Sunday on a four-day official visit to Bangladesh. He is accompanied by senior officials and a large team of Thai entrepreneurs.
"Unfortunately, we could not put due attention to this region because of frequent changes in government (in Bangkok). But we think it's not too late," said Intrawityanunt.
India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka have a combined population of nearly one billion.
Thai diplomats in Dhaka said the minister's visit to Bangladesh was in pursuance of Bangkok's new "Look West" policy.
Intrawityanunt, who took office four months ago, has already visited Sri Lanka and plans to visit India next month.

One Bangladesh official said the Thai effort could face a cold response with Thailand tightening visa procedures for visitors from some SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) countries, including Bangladesh.
The restriction came in the face of strong complaints from Malaysia that illegal immigrants from South Asia use Bangkok as corridor.
News reports in Dhaka said recently that some 50,000 Bangladeshis, willing to enter Malaysia for job, were in Thai jungles bordering Malaysia.
The minister, however, said there were only "few thousand" illegal Bangladeshis in Thai territory. Of them, he said, about 1,000 were awaiting deportation.
Intrawityanunt said small irritants should not overshadow relations and genuine visitors would never be hit by the visa restriction.
The minister said Bangkok was particularly keen for improved trade and investment ties with Bangladesh, the country he termed as "gateway to this (South Asia) region".
Bangladesh and Thailand currently transact a modest volume of trade with the balance heavily tilting towards Bangkok.
Two-way trade amounted to $124 million in 1996 with Thailand exporting goods worth $105 million.
"The (trade) figures are very very poor," said Intrawityanunt, adding that both governments wanted to raise the total to at least $400 million by year 2000.
Some 13 Thai companies have invested $25 million in Bangladesh.
The minister said Thailand was eager to relocate labour-intensive industries to Bangladesh to take advantage of abundant cheap labour.

In talks during last two days, officials and entrepreneurs of Bangladesh and Thailand agreed on joint venture investment in a wide range of sectors including textile garments, poultry, fisheries, construction and energy.
Dhaka and Bangkok signed a deal on Sunday on avoidance of double taxation
Intrawityanunt expressed optimism that the incumbent government in Dhaka was pursuing the "right" economic policy which, he said, would lead Bangladesh towards faster development.
"You are in the right direction. I will admire the positive effort of the visionary leadership," he said.
